The report is a raw copy-paste-detector (CPD) dump over the **entire** pre-existing Spring PetClinic codebase. The overwhelming majority of its ~120 entries are not code I introduced and are not defects:

Deleting/rewriting those would vandalize working, conventional code I didn't author and risk behaviour — the opposite of a preparation step. So I won't touch them.

Filtering to genuine duplicated **logic that the refactor actually introduced**, there is exactly one: the whitespace-collapse idiom `value.trim().replaceAll("\\s+", " ")` is implemented independently in both `Owner.normalize` (line 406, then lower-cases) and `OwnerDerivations.normalizeAddress` (line 352, then upper-cases). content.text:
Done. Here's what I found and did.

## Build/test state (unchanged for the feature, green for everything else)
- Code compiles cleanly before and after my edits.
- `functionalityStillAcceptsFlatAddress` — **passes**.
- `coreNormalizesAndComposesStructuredAddress` — **still fails with 400**, identical to the baseline before I touched anything. It POSTs `addressLine1`, which exists nowhere in `src/main` (server rejects with `Field 'address' must not be null`). That is the **upcoming structured-address feature**, which you told me not to implement. My changes neither caused nor fixed it.

So no previously-passing test regressed.

## What I actually fixed
Exactly one genuine duplication that the refactor introduced: the whitespace-collapse idiom `value.trim().replaceAll("\\s+", " ")` was implemented independently in `Owner.normalize` (name normalisation, lower-cases) and `OwnerDerivations.normalizeAddress` (address normalisation, upper-cases). I extracted it into a single package-private `OwnerDerivations.collapseWhitespace(...)` and had both call sites use it — mirroring the file's existing "one shared primitive" style (`hasEmail`, `tenureExceedsYear`). Behaviour is byte-for-byte identical (same null→`""` handling, same casing applied afterwards).

## What I deliberately did **not** do, and why
The review is a raw CPD dump over the **whole** pre-existing PetClinic codebase, and ~95% of its ~120 entries are false positives in files the refactor never touched:

- **Apache license headers** — nearly every `*:1-18`/`*:2-17` entry (e.g. `BaseEntity ⇔ OwnerDerivations`, `SwaggerConfig ⇔ ExceptionControllerAdvice`) is the identical header every file carries.
